folds.title: Hallucinations
points: A **hallucination** is an answer that sounds sure but is wrong.
Typical culprits: made-up quotes, invented web links and wrong dates.
Also books or studies that do not exist.
Odd, specific details are the riskiest.

folds.title: The book that is not real
points: You ask for three books about beekeeping.
Claude lists three, with authors and years.
Two are real. The third sounds just right, but does not exist.
folds.note: A quick search for each title catches it.

folds.title: How to check
items: Ask Claude where a fact comes from, then open that source yourself.
Compare with a trusted website or a second source.
Check names, numbers and quotes first.

folds.title: Trust, but check
points: Treat Claude like a smart colleague, not a source of truth.
The more it matters, the more you check.
Take extra care with health, money, legal and school work.

folds.prompt: One part of this answer is made up. Tap it.

segments.text: Paris is the capital of France.
The Eiffel Tower is in Paris.
It was designed by Leonardo da Vinci.
It is made mostly of iron.

folds.why: The tower was built by Gustave Eiffel's company, not da Vinci. Claude can sound sure and still be wrong.
